newsitem.title: BULGARIA: PRESS DIGEST - Bulgaria - Oct 10. [CORRECTED 10:04 GMT]
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bulgaria - Oct 10. [CORRECTED 10:04 GMT]

text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Bulgaria's monthly consumer price inflation accelerated to 18.8 percent in September from 17.1 percent in August and cumulative inflation rose to 153 percent since January 1, the National Statistics Institute said.
-- Interior Minister Nikilay Dobrev said his ministry did not have a list of Bulgaria's credit millionaires, denying local media reports that such a list had been presented to the cabinet.

-- U.S. firm Amoco Corp will sell its retail petrol stations in Bulgaria, Romania and Poland as a part of a strategy to remain competitive in the global petrol market, the head of Amoco's Bulgarian branch, James Shields, said.
-- Bulgaria has launched liquidation procedures for 10 of its 38 debt-ridden industrial firms earmarked for closure by the cabinet, Industry Minister Lyubomir Dachev said.

-- By the end of the year, Bulgaria is expected to sell 30 of the 56 big state-owned enterprises earmarked by the cabinet for urgent privatisation, Privatisation Agency executive director Vesselin Blagoev said at the end of a visit to Washington.

-- Bulgaria is expected to import some 100,000-200,000 tonnes of wheat from Kazakhstan in exchange for forgiving part of Kazakhstan's debt to the state-owned Glavbolgarstroy construction firm, deputy premier Doncho Konakchiev said.
-- Bulgaria will have to pay 28 million levs to the international auditing company Deloitte & Touche for performing the audit of the Bulgarian National Bank, the BNB said.

-- Kremlin officials have refused to meet the presidential candidates for the ruling Socialist Party, Ivan Marazov and Irina Bokova, if they visit Moscow, the newspaper said without quoting sources. It said the candidates asked for the visit after the main opposition presidential candidate Petar Stoyanov met senior government officials in Germany and Poland.
-- Bankers from the 14 banks which the central bank has put under special supervision are banned from leaving the country, chief prosecutor Ivan Tatarchev said.

-- Macedonia's president Kiro Gligorov met a visiting delegation from Bulgaria's largest private conglomerate Multigroup to discuss its investments in his country and prospects for further development, Balkan news agency said.
